title: QUIZ - 15
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.concept: Reverse Percentage Word Problems
questions.learningObjective: Determine a total amount from a known part and its percentage in context
questions.question: If 69 represents 40% of a company's total revenue in thousands of dollars, what is the total value (rounded to two decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Since 69 is 40% of the total, the total is \(69 \div 0.4 = 172.5\).
questions.hint: Divide the given part by the percentage expressed as a decimal to find the whole.

questions.concept: Finding the Whole from a Percentage
questions.learningObjective: Find the original whole amount when a part and its percentage are known
questions.question: 108 is 40% of what number?
questions.explanation: Let the unknown value be x. Then \(40/100 \times x = 108\), so \(x = 108 \div (40/100) = 270\).
questions.hint: Divide the known part by the percentage written as a decimal.

questions.concept: Finding the Whole from a Percentage
questions.learningObjective: Find the original whole amount when a part and its percentage are known
questions.question: 1 is 10% of what number?
questions.explanation: Let the unknown value be x. Then \(10/100 \times x = 1\), so \(x = 1 \div (10/100) = 10\).
questions.hint: Divide the known part by the percentage written as a decimal.

questions.concept: Multi-Step Reverse Percentage Problems
questions.learningObjective: Apply reverse percentage reasoning across two nested percentage relationships
questions.question: After applying a discount, a store manager notes that 180 units sold represent 24% of total inventory. If 180 is 24% of the inventory, and the inventory itself is 24% of a regional total, what is the regional total (rounded to the nearest whole number)?
questions.explanation: First find the inventory: \(180 \div 0.24 = 750\). Then find the regional total: \(750 \div 0.24 \approx 3125\).
questions.hint: Work backwards one percentage step at a time, dividing by the decimal form of each percentage.
